title: Maintenance assignment review
description: review_schedule(request) validates the entire request or raises ValueError without mutating it; exception text is not fixed. It returns equipment_count (number of equipment items), requirement_count (number of raw requirement records), current, proposed and changes. Each of current/proposed contains windows, conflict_weight, separated_weight and conflicts. A conflict is a positive-total-weight equipment pair assigned to the same window. Repeated/reversed requirements add weights; zero-total pairs are omitted from conflict lists. conflict_weight sums same-window weights; separated_weight sums different-window weights. Proposed windows must globally minimize conflict_weight. Ties choose the smallest sum of 2**i over equipment input positions i in window 0, regardless of the current arrangement; minimum movement is NOT an objective. All output windows list names in equipment input order, even if input current_windows used another order. Conflict records have first, second and weight; endpoints and records are ordered by their equipment positions i<j, then increasing (i,j). changes contains moved_equipment (records with equipment, from_window, to_window, ordered by equipment input order; window indices are 0 and 1), conflict_reduction (current minus proposed conflict_weight), resolved_conflicts (current conflict records absent in proposed), and introduced_conflicts (proposed conflict records absent in current). The latter lists retain conflict ordering. Conflicts that remain are exactly proposed.conflicts. Zero improvement does not imply no moves. Empty equipment requires current_windows=[[],[]] and yields empty lists and zero scores/counts. The valid JSON CLI reads one request from stdin and prints one report; invalid input produces no successful report and a nonzero exit. No approximate score, arbitrary tie choice, input mutation or omitted reporting is permitted.
